title: Flatness of the canonical affine strict henselization structural ring map
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $H$ its canonical pointed-neighbourhood coordinate-ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. If $b:R\to H$ induces the canonical structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], then $b$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tags 04HX and 07QM; Tag 0EYG, first reduction paragraph. Lean colimit argument uses WeilConjectures.RingTheory.ProEtale.FaithfullyFlat, RingHom.Flat.of_isColimit (lines 255-263).

proof.text: The representative pointed-neighbourhood category is cofiltered. Opposite it gives a small filtered ring diagram. The maps from R to its stages are GammaSpecIso(R).inv followed by the neighbourhood structure morphism on global sections. The over-category equations and contravariant global sections make these maps a natural transformation.
Every neighbourhood is etale over Spec R, hence its map on global sections is flat. Precomposition with GammaSpecIso(R).inv preserves flatness, since that is a ring isomorphism.

The defining common-composite characterization of the structural morphism identifies each stage map followed by the colimit coprojection with b. This is proved using Spec.map_injective, GammaSpecIso_inv_naturality and hb. Apply RingHom.Flat.of_isColimit, the forward implication of the existing ind-flat characterization, to this filtered diagram.

theorem strictHenselization_structural_ringHom_flat
    (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R)
    (b : R ⟶ strictHenselization barY)
    (hb : Spec.map b = strictLocalizationToBase barY) :
    RingHom.Flat b.hom
lean.note: Retirement of the Sheaf twin, as requested by coord/retire-items.tsv. The adopted source theorem proves flatness for the upstream strictHenselization and strictLocalizationToBase. The original small-representative colimit is canonically isomorphic by smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso. A compiled verification checks that Spec of this comparison followed by strictHenselizationStructuralMap is strictLocalizationToBase, and transports source flatness back to the exact original small-ring statement. The four archived Sheaf consumers and their DAG dependency edges are preserved; their active source counterparts already import and apply this upstream theorem.
